topology_reasoning.device_identification: The image shows a primitives-level adiabatic 1x2 splitter/trident. A central input guide enters from the left, holds a short constant-width section, then tapers down to a narrow terminal tip. Two disconnected upper/lower guides begin as narrow tips near the same x position, adiabatically widen beside the central taper, then follow smooth S-bends to separated output rails at the upper and lower edges of the footprint.
topology_reasoning.operating_principle: The central taper gradually transfers the input mode into the two widening side branches while keeping gaps and taper angles small enough for adiabatic splitting. The S-bends then fan the two branches out into output ports without changing the guide width.
topology_reasoning.parametric_strategy: Use only straight path extrusions, taper primitives, and sampled gf.Path extrusions. The central material is a fixed-width straight plus a taper; each side branch is a taper followed by a smooth cosine S-bend and output straight. The delta_length knob extends only the upper output rail for verify_knob_response while the baseline remains matched to the image.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only trident/Y-splitter model. Diff review showed residual bend-shape mismatch: red on outer bend edges and blue on inner bend edges, but IoU exceeded the 0.85 Phase A threshold and footprint matched exactly, so no further geometry changes were made.
